sources.label: GitHub Actions — Events that trigger workflows (workflow_run: GITHUB_SHA = last commit on default branch)
sources.summary: workflow_run sets GITHUB_SHA to the LAST COMMIT ON THE DEFAULT BRANCH and GITHUB_REF to the default branch — NOT the commit CI validated. conclusion-based gating via github.event.workflow_run.conclusion is documented. This is the root of the SHA hazard the design fixes.

sources.label: actions/checkout README — ref default (event ref/SHA else default branch)
sources.summary: ref: 'When checking out the repository that triggered a workflow, this defaults to the reference or SHA for that event. Otherwise, uses the default branch.' For workflow_run that resolves to default-branch HEAD. Design's explicit ref: github.event.workflow_run.head_sha is the correct fix.

sources.label: actions/checkout input-helper.ts — default ref resolution falls back to github.context.ref/sha
sources.summary: When no explicit ref and target is the workflow repo, sets result.ref=github.context.ref, result.commit=github.context.sha. For workflow_run these are default-branch values.

sources.label: actions/checkout unsafe-pr-checkout-helper.ts — confirms workflow_run payload paths
sources.summary: Source reads workflow_run.event (string), workflow_run.head_sha, workflow_run.head_branch, workflow_run.head_commit.id — confirms the design's conclusion/head_branch/event checks reference valid properties. Also: 'For pull_request_target-triggered workflow_run, head_sha is the base default branch SHA (not the PR head)' — motivates event=='push' filter.

sources.label: Sawtaytoes/mux-magic commit 1016904 — real-world identical bug class under workflow_run
sources.summary: 'Under a workflow_run trigger, github.sha (and github.ref) resolve to the default branch (master), not the branch whose CI run triggered the deploy. So feat/** builds were checked out from master HEAD ... the image's code never matched its tag.' Fixed by using github.event.workflow_run.head_sha. Exact same defect class as lgrep's auto-release.

sources.label: po4erk91/thread-keeper commit f83b559 — detached-HEAD + main-advance race under workflow_run
sources.summary: Documents checkout@v6 ref=head_sha lands in detached-HEAD state and that pinning ref=main instead carries a 'tiny race window if main moves between tests passing and release running.' Confirms detached-HEAD and push-back-race concerns for lgrep's changelog-commit-then-push-to-main pattern.

sources.label: actions/checkout issue #1418 — default-branch checkout behavior for non-push triggers
sources.summary: Maintainer confirmation github.sha is captured at run-start and stable across a run; default checkout uses github context ref/sha. Supports that only an explicit ref builds the CI-validated commit under workflow_run.

sources.label: Local: .github/workflows/auto-release.yml — current checkout has NO ref; tag on a NEW changelog commit; git push origin HEAD:head_branch
sources.summary: Current job uses actions/checkout@v4 fetch-depth:0 but NO ref => checks out default-branch HEAD. Tag is created on a NEW changelog commit on top of the checkout, then git push origin HEAD:head_branch + git push tag. Under the design's ref=head_sha this commit-push becomes detached-HEAD, non-fast-forward-risk.

sources.label: Local: .github/workflows/ci.yml — triggers on push:main AND pull_request:main
sources.summary: PR-triggered CI runs have head_branch != main and are filtered by Auto Release branches:[main]; push-to-main runs trigger. Design's explicit event=='push' check is sound defense-in-depth.

sources.label: Local: pyproject.toml — hatch-vcs version derivation
sources.summary: Version VCS-derived via hatch-vcs; [project.scripts] lgrep=lgrep.cli:main is the console entry. tag-pattern 'v(?P<version>.*)' + version_scheme 'no-guess-dev' means a tag at the exact SHA yields exactly X.Y.Z. Supports design's tag-before-build claim, contingent on the proposed fixture verifying it.

sources.label: Local: ~/.config/vision/servers.yaml — lgrep runtime is /home/jon/.local/bin/lgrep console script
sources.summary: Vision lgrep server: command /home/jon/.local/bin/lgrep, port 6278, stdio subprocess republished on HTTP. Confirms design's '~/.local/bin' runtime claim and that a deploy must replace the uv-tool-installed console script. Health proof 'through Vision' = real MCP call to the running daemon on 6278.

sources.label: Local: src/lgrep/server/tools_maintenance.py + responses.py — MCP prune responses carry non-nullable string refused_reason
sources.summary: MCP handlers prune_orphans/prune_symbols add refused_reason via setdefault ('' on success, message on destructive-downgrade). responses.py declares refused_reason: str on PruneOrphansResult/PruneSymbolsResult. Resolves AC4: 'string refused_reason' is the real contract; EMPTY string == healthy preview.

sources.label: Local: tests/test_mcp_response_contract.py — refused_reason enforced non-nullable string, '' on default path
sources.summary: test_maintenance_output_schema_rejects_nullable_refused_reason asserts refused_reason schema == {type:string}; test_maintenance_tool_validates_on_default_path asserts refused_reason=='' for dry_run=True. Health-proof success criterion is refused_reason=='' (empty), i.e. clean non-destructive preview.

sources.label: Local: src/lgrep/tools/prune_symbols.py + prune_orphans.py — dry_run=True default, non-destructive
sources.summary: Both prune functions default dry_run=True and only delete when dry_run=False; dry-run returns projected reclaim with deleted_files/deleted_dirs=0. The two-call health proof is genuinely non-destructive and satisfies C3 when dry_run=True.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Core design is correct and well-sourced. (1) workflow_run + actions/checkout-without-ref checks out DEFAULT-BRANCH HEAD, not the CI-validated commit — verified against the GitHub events doc (workflow_run GITHUB_SHA = 'last commit on default branch'), actions/checkout source (input-helper.ts falls back to github.context.sha), a real-world identical bug (Sawtaytoes/mux-magic), and the current auto-release.yml (no ref). The design's ref: github.event.workflow_run.head_sha is the canonical fix. (2) The design's conclusion/head_branch/event checks all reference valid github.event.workflow_run.* properties (confirmed by actions/checkout unsafe-pr-checkout-helper.ts reading workflow_run.event/head_sha/head_branch/head_commit). (3) Tag-before-build + hatch-vcs no-guess-dev yields exactly X.Y.Z at the tagged SHA (pyproject.toml). (4) The Vision runtime is /home/jon/.local/bin/lgrep (servers.yaml), so a uv-tool install/upgrade is the right deploy mechanism; health proof via two dry_run=True prune previews is genuinely non-destructive (C3) and the MCP contract carries refused_reason as a non-nullable string ('' on success). Three correctness-affecting clarifications remain before the design is airtight.

validation.notes: No hard blockers; core design is sound and externally verified. CAUTION because three in-scope clarifications affect AC1 and deploy-path correctness and should be resolved before execution/planning: (a) AC1 'zero-job outcomes are treated as failure evidence' must distinguish a SPURIOUS zero-job (workflow_run fired but no job selected/executed — the original defect) from the LEGITIMATE no-release-needed skip path (steps.bump.outputs.skip=='true' gates all release steps — an intentional zero-action). The detection fixture must assert selectability for a valid event WITH version-worthy commits AND keep the benign skip distinguishable, or the failure signal false-positives on chore-only pushes. (b) Checking out head_sha lands the repo in DETACHED HEAD; the current changelog-commit + 'git push origin HEAD:head_branch' then becomes a non-fast-forward risk if main advanced between CI and release (po4erk91/thread-keeper documents exactly this race). Design should make explicit: tag head_sha directly (sufficient for version derivation — the build does not need the changelog commit), and either make the CHANGELOG push-back best-effort/optional or drop it from the release-critical path. (c) Auto Release publishes to GitHub Releases via softprops/action-gh-release, NOT to PyPI (no twine/pypi step). lgrep is not installable from PyPI, so the deploy install source must be explicit: either the GitHub release wheel asset URL (uv tool install --from <release-url>) or a local build from the checked-out tag (uv tool install ./dist/*.whl). AC3 'installs the selected/tagged lgrep artifact' leaves this open.

tradeoffs: workflow_run + explicit head_sha checkout fixes an existing, externally-verified defect class (default-branch-HEAD release) but adds detached-HEAD + push-back-race complexity vs an in-workflow release job.

Two-call dry_run prune health proof is non-destructive (satisfies C3) but only proves the daemon answers and the schema validates; the version check (AC4 first clause) separately proves the installed CLI is the intended release.
Non-nullable string refused_reason (empty==healthy) is robust against strict-schema clients but requires the health proof to assert =='' rather than merely 'present'.
Tagging head_sha directly gives exact version derivation but decouples the release tag from the CHANGELOG commit, so the changelog must land via a separate/best-effort path.

alternatives_considered.option: Merge the release job into ci.yml on push:branches:[main] gated by needs:[lint,test] and if:github.event_name=='push'
alternatives_considered.rationale: On a push event GITHUB_SHA IS the exact pushed commit, so actions/checkout with no ref already checks out the validated commit — eliminating the entire detached-HEAD/head_sha hazard (P19 simplicity). Tradeoff: couples publish to the CI workflow file and loses the separate verify-vs-publish workflow separation; merging is more churn against an already-deployed workflow_run file. Defensible to keep workflow_run now that the head_sha fix is known-correct, but this should be a conscious choice.

alternatives_considered.option: Pin ref to branch name 'main' instead of head_sha (po4erk91/thread-keeper approach)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Reintroduces the race the design is specifically trying to close (build from main HEAD that may have advanced past the CI-validated commit). head_sha is the correct immutable source.

alternatives_considered.option: Publish to PyPI and have the deploy do 'uv tool install lgrep==X.Y.Z'
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would require adding twine/PyPI trusted-publishing and is larger than the contract contemplates; the GitHub-Release wheel source (or local build from tag) is the in-scope path.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to planning AFTER the design text is amended with: (1) explicit AC1 distinction between spurious-zero-job (failure) and intentional skip (benign), with the fixture asserting job-selectability for a valid event carrying version-worthy commits; (2) detached-HEAD handling — tag head_sha directly for version derivation and demote the CHANGELOG commit/push to best-effort or a separate step, citing the non-fast-forward race; (3) explicit deploy install source (GitHub-release wheel URL or local build from the checked-out tag), since lgrep is not on PyPI. With those three amendments the design is PASS-grade.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Approve the design with CAUTION and the three amendments above. Core fixes (head_sha checkout, payload-property gating, tag-before-build, trunk-only uv-tool deploy, two non-destructive dry_run prune previews asserting refused_reason=='') are all correct and externally verified. Resolve the AC1 skip-vs-spurious distinction, detached-HEAD push-back race, and PyPI-vs-release-asset install source in the design text before the design gate is marked done. Also verify the exact systemd unit/CLI for the restart (design says 'vision.service'; confirm systemctl --user unit name or 'vision daemon restart') as an implementation detail.
follow_ups: Scope-key note: the packet supplied SCOPE KEY 'design:release-local-deploy' but the typed report schema requires the researcher: prefix, so scope_key was normalized to 'researcher:release-local-deploy'.

Confirm 'no-guess-dev' is accepted by the installed hatch-vcs/setuptools_scm version at build time (the proposed AC2 wheel-metadata fixture is the authoritative check; flag only if the fixture fails).
Confirm the systemd user-unit name / restart command for Vision (design says vision.service) before execution.
Decide whether the simpler in-ci.yml release-job alternative (push event, needs:[lint,test]) is worth the churn vs keeping the corrected workflow_run approach — conscious choice, not blocking.

items.text: **Runnable release trigger** — a completed successful `CI` workflow on `main` creates an Auto Release run with at least one executable release job; zero-job outcomes are treated as failure evidence.
**Exact release source** — Auto Release checks out `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha`, creates `vX.Y.Z` before building, and publishes wheel/sdist whose metadata is exactly `X.Y.Z`.

**Safe local deploy command** — one documented command/script, executed only from clean merged `main`, installs the selected/tagged lgrep artifact into Vision's configured runtime, validates Vision configuration, and restarts the user service.

**Real local health proof** — the deploy path confirms the installed CLI version equals the selected release and runs `prune_symbols` plus `prune_orphans` through Vision; both must return successful structured results with string `refused_reason`.
**Bounded startup handling** — one bounded initialization retry is allowed after a service restart; persistent initialization/health failure exits nonzero and reports the failing step.
**Release safety** — no local deploy claims healthy before all health checks pass; failed release runs or deployment checks are discoverable through CI output or command exit status.
Do not deploy/rebuild from a worktree.
Do not auto-delete caches or grant destructive maintenance operations.

rows.evidence: Static workflow fixture tests verify valid main-push CI event selects the release job; invalid events produce detectable failure. Schema-validated YAML. Empirical post-merge proof pending.
Tests verify checkout uses workflow_run.head_sha and tag is created before build. Wheel metadata derives from tag via Hatch VCS.
Deploy command refuses non-trunk/dirty/untagged source; installs GitHub Release wheel; validates Vision config; restarts service. 23 unit tests cover safety paths.
Reviewer verified live Vision prune_symbols and prune_orphans return refused_reason='' through real MCP transport with corrected Accept header.
Deploy command implements one bounded initialization retry; persistent failure exits nonzero with step-specific output. Unit tests cover retry and failure paths.
Deploy command exits nonzero on any unhealthy step; worktree dry-run correctly refused. Full suite 800 passed.
Tag-before-build preserved; workflow tags head_sha before python -m build.
Deploy command refuses worktree branches; all code work in ADV worktree.
Health checks use dry_run=true only; no destructive operations.

# Fix auto release trigger

## Why

Updating lgrep should publish and become a healthy local Vision service without manual recovery.

## What Changes

- Make successful `main` CI trigger a runnable release job.
- Preserve tag-before-build artifact identity.
- Add a documented/automated local deployment step that installs the tagged artifact, restarts Vision, and verifies version plus representative MCP calls.
- Make initialization and health failures explicit, bounded, and non-successful.

## Success

- [ ] Successful `main` CI creates a runnable Auto Release job.
- [ ] The release job tags before building and publishes tag-matched assets.
- [ ] A local update installs the intended release, restarts Vision, and verifies the service version and two maintenance MCP previews.
- [ ] No local deployment reports healthy until those real MCP calls pass.
- [ ] Zero-job release failures and local health failures have automated detectable evidence.
documents.problemStatement:
# Release-to-local deployment health failure

## Root Cause Analysis

Automatic publishing is unreliable: the `Auto Release` workflow configured for successful `main` CI records zero-job failures instead of running its release job. This forced a manual v3.2.4 tag/build/publish.

Local deployment is also manual and opaque: installing a new lgrep tool environment plus restarting Vision required operator steps, and the first post-restart MCP request can fail during initialization. There is no deployment-owned health check proving the managed Vision lgrep server loaded the intended version and accepts representative structured-content calls before operators treat the update as healthy.

These are one delivery-path defect: a successful release must create a tag-matched artifact and then update/restart/check the local Vision service deterministically, with failures visible and no claim of health before real MCP verification.

# Agreement: Fix release-to-local deployment health

## Objective

Make a successful `main` CI run publish a tag-matched lgrep release and give operators one deterministic local Vision update path with real health proof.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Runnable release trigger** — a completed successful `CI` workflow on `main` creates an Auto Release run with at least one executable release job; zero-job outcomes are treated as failure evidence.
2. **Exact release source** — Auto Release checks out `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha`, creates `vX.Y.Z` before building, and publishes wheel/sdist whose metadata is exactly `X.Y.Z`.
3. **Safe local deploy command** — one documented command/script, executed only from clean merged `main`, installs the selected/tagged lgrep artifact into Vision's configured runtime, validates Vision configuration, and restarts the user service.
4. **Real local health proof** — the deploy path confirms the installed CLI version equals the selected release and runs `prune_symbols` plus `prune_orphans` through Vision; both must return successful structured results with string `refused_reason`.
5. **Bounded startup handling** — one bounded initialization retry is allowed after a service restart; persistent initialization/health failure exits nonzero and reports the failing step.
6. **Release safety** — no local deploy claims healthy before all health checks pass; failed release runs or deployment checks are discoverable through CI output or command exit status.

## Constraints

- Preserve tag-before-build version derivation.
- Do not deploy/rebuild from a worktree.
- Do not auto-delete caches or grant destructive maintenance operations.

## Evidence

- Workflow fixture/static validation plus a successful downstream release run.
- Local deploy dry-run or controlled test plus real Vision verification after a tagged release.
documents.design:
# Design: Release-to-local deployment health

## CI release trigger

Use `workflow_run` only for completed successful `CI` push runs on `main`. The release job explicitly checks `conclusion == 'success'`, `head_branch == 'main'`, and `event == 'push'`. It checks out `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha`, tags that exact SHA directly before building, and never relies on ambient default-branch HEAD.

A workflow fixture distinguishes a valid version-worthy triggering event (release job must be selectable) from an intentional no-release-needed outcome. Spurious zero-job/non-selectable valid events fail validation. CHANGELOG generation is separate/best-effort: it must not make the tag/build/release depend on a detached-HEAD push-back race.

## Local deployment command

Add a trunk-only deploy command that refuses non-trunk, dirty, untagged, or missing-release source. It downloads/installs the selected GitHub Release wheel URL into Vision's configured uv-tool runtime, validates Vision configuration, restarts `vision.service`, and checks installed CLI version.

It runs two non-destructive Vision MCP previews. One initialization retry is permitted after restart; persistent initialization/health error exits nonzero with step-specific output.

## Invariants

- Worktrees may test but never deploy.
- Release tag, source SHA, and artifacts match.
- Local success means real Vision calls pass.
- No destructive maintenance operation runs.
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary: Fix auto release trigger

## Outcome

lgrep releases now trigger deterministically from successful main CI, and operators have one safe local deployment command with real Vision health proof.

## Why It Matters

Eliminates the zero-job release failure that forced manual v3.2.4 publication. Operators can update Vision and verify health without manual recovery steps.

## Verdict

APPROVED

## What Was Built

1. Auto Release workflow now checks out the exact triggering CI SHA, tags before building, and uses correct GitHub Actions YAML (block scalar for release files).
2. Added a safe Vision deploy command (`scripts/deploy_vision.py`) that refuses non-trunk/dirty source, installs tagged release wheels, restarts Vision, verifies CLI version, and runs non-destructive MCP health checks with bounded retry.
3. CHANGELOG generation restored as a post-release best-effort step from origin/main.

## What Was Verified

- Verdict: APPROVED with 3 blockers found and fixed by reviewer (workflow YAML regression, test shape assertion, MCP Accept header)
- Tests: 800 passed, Ruff clean
- Preview URL: not_applicable — backend automation and CLI tooling
- Contract matrix: 6 AC pass, 3 constraints respected
- Live Vision prune calls verified by reviewer with corrected Accept header

## Remaining Concerns

- AC1/AC2 empirical proof requires a real post-merge release run; static and schema validation is the pre-merge ceiling.
- AC3/AC5 deploy command unit tests are mock-based; real deployment verification occurs post-merge.
- `action-gh-release@v2` uses deprecated Node 20 runner — non-blocking follow-up.

## Supporting Evidence

- Task tk-211aea8c7d3d: workflow YAML fix + fixture tests (10 tests)
- Task tk-5ad7d7b8cd00: deploy command + 23 unit tests + docs
- Reviewer report: 3 blockers fixed, live Vision verification, 800 tests
- Checkpoint SHA: 76f010cfd36608823faad1adac9ba32e9ded2bef
